sentences.text: 1 The petitioner has filed this claim petition against the respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest for the injuries sustained by her in a Road Traffic Accident.

2. The brief contents of the petition are as under:
On 21.04.2021 at about 11.30 am., when the petitioner was riding NTRO125 Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-03-JV-2333 on left side of the double road of Indiranagar slowly cautiously by observing road traffic rules and after crossing the Siradi Saibaba road,
Indiranagar double road ESI Hospital quarters junction signal, at that time, the driver of one Baleno alpha Car bearing reg.No.KA-53-MG-0063 came from Dommalur SCCH - 9 3 MVC No.3886/2021 to Shanthinagar Hotel junction side without observing traffic rules and hit to the rearside of the petitioner's vehicle.
Due to said impact, the petitioner and her scooter fell down and petitioner sustained multiple fractured injuries.

Thereafter, the petitioner was took the treatment at Manipal Hospital as an inpatient and spent Rs.2,40,000/- towards medical expenses,
conveyance and nourishment and attended charges etc.,

Prior to the accident,
petitioner was working as Funds Raiser and due to the injuries sustained she is not able to do the job and any job in future as before the accident and surgery is required to her nose and face.
The Halsur Traffic police have registered a case in crime No.15/2021 under Section 279, 337, 338 of IPC against the driver of Baleno alpha Car bearing reg.No.KA-53-MG-0063.

The 1 st respondent being the RC owner and 2nd r e s p o n d e n t b e i n g t h e I n s u r e r o f t h e B a l e n o a l p h a C a r b e a r i n g reg.No.KA-53-MG-0063 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to SCCH - 9 4 MVC No.3886/2021 the petitioner.

Hence, on all these grounds, the petitioner prayed to allow this petition and award compensation of Rs.20,00,000/-
under all heads together with interest and costs.

3. In response to the Court notice, the respondent No.1 and respondent No.2 has appeared before the court through its counsel and only respondent No.2 has filed the written statement.
4.

The brief contentions of the written statement of respondent No.2 are as under:
The respondent contended that, petition is not maintainable in law, facts and circumstances of the case and petition is liable to be dismissed against this respondent.
Respondent denied the place, date and time of alleged accident and also denied the income and avocation of the petitioner.

Respondent contended that,
compensation claimed by the petitioner is exorbitant.
Further contended that, driver of the car was not holding a valid and effective driving licence at the time SCCH - 9 5 MVC No.3886/2021 of accident.

Further the respondent No.2 has contended that,
the owner of the vehicle and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of M.V.Act.

It has contended that, the petitioner Chandrakala vs Darshan.N.Nagendra on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45467252/
2 is working as NGO and the employer is given the medical allowance to the petitioner and the medical bills amount reimbursed.

Further it is the contention of the respondent that, the petitioner has lodged the complaint after the lapse of 6 days after the accident.
Further contended that, the policy obtained by the first respondent from the second respondent is private car stand alone own damage policy not to third party.

Hence,
on all these contentions, the respondent No.2 prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues have been framed :
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner SCCH - 9 6 MVC No.3886/2021 proves that, she has sustained injuries on account of Road Traffic Accident took place on 21.04.2021 at about 11.30 a.m at Sai Baba Temple Road and Indiranagar double road, near ESI Hospital Junction, Indiranagara, Bengaluru due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Baleno alpha Car bearing Reg. KA53MG0063 by its driver?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3.

What Order or Award?
6.
In order to prove the case, the petitioner examined herself as PW-1 and got marked the 14 documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.14.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has not adduced any oral or documentary evidences.

7. Heard arguments from petitioner and respondent and I have perused the records.
8.

My findings to the above issues as follows:
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative  Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3: As per final order,

ISSUE NO.1: It is the case of the petitioner that, on 21.04.2021 at about 11.30 am., when she was riding NTRO125 Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-03-JV-2333 on left side of the double road of Indiranagar slowly cautiously by observing Chandrakala vs Darshan.N.Nagendra on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45467252/
3 road traffic rules and after crossing the Siradi Saibaba road, Indiranagar double road ESI Hospital quarters junction signal, at that time, the driver of one Baleno alpha Car bearing reg.No.KA- 53-MG-0063 came from Dommalur to Shanthinagar Hotel junction side without observing traffic rules and hit to the rearside of her vehicle.
Due to said impact, she and her scooter fell down and she sustained multiple fractured injuries.

10. To prove the accident that occurred due to the sole negligence on the part of the driver of the offending Car, the petitioner herself got examined as PW-1 and got marked the documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.14.
Perused the police document i.e., Ex.P.1 is the FIR, Ex.P.2 is the complaint, Ex.P.3 is the charge sheet, SCCH - 9 8 MVC No.3886/2021 Ex.P.4 is the spot panchanama and Ex.P.5 is the spot sketch.
11. On perusal of above said documents the owner of the offending Car have not disputed involvement of vehicles.
The respondent No.2 counsel suggested to the PW-1 as accident was occurred due to her own negligence, but witness has denied the said suggestion.

Therefore, by considering the oral and documentary evidence on record and above discussion, I am of the opinion that, the accident was occurred on negligence of driver of the offending Car bearing reg.No.KA-53-MG-0063.
The petitioner has produced the wound certificate as per Ex.P.6, that document discloses the petitioner has sustained grievous injury.
Hence, I answer the Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:- In view of answering issue No.1 in the affirmative the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

To assess the compensation the Tribunal has to look into several facts like injuries,
pain and suffering sustained by the petitioner and amount spent SCCH - 9 9 MVC No.3886/2021 by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment, medical and attendant,
charges, conveyance, loss of income during treatment, disability, loss of amenities etc., let me discuss one by one:
a) TOWARDS INJURY, PAIN AND SUFFERING:
The petitioner has contended that immediately after the accident, she was shifted to Manipal Hospital wherein she took treatment as an inpatient and during the course of treatment X-rays were taken which revealed that the petitioner sustained abrasion over right side face, abrasion over right forearm, abrasion over front of right knee,
abrasion over right shoulder, swelling and tenderness over right orbit, swelling and tenderness over right maxilla, swelling and tenderness over right nose: inferior wall of right orbit fracture, right maxillary sinus fracture, nasal bone fracture and injuries 5 to 7 are grievous in nature.

Further, Manipal Hospital discharge summary reveals that, investigation summary C.T Brain with C, spine and facial cuts, inferior wall of right orbit fracture, right maxillary sinus fracture, nasal SCCH - 9 10 MVC No.3886/2021 bone fracture and traumatic facial fracture and took treatment at Hosmat Hospital and Chinmaya mission Hospital, Bengaluru and advised to take bed rest.

In order to prove injuries caused to her she has produced wound certificate/Ex.P6, which reveals that petitioner has sustained simple as well as Chandrakala vs Darshan.N.Nagendra on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45467252/
4 grievous injuries in nature.

sentences.text: The petitioner has not examined doctor to prove the disability.
As the petitioner sustained simple injury and considering the avocation of the petitioner it is just and proper to award the compensation of Rs.30,000/- under the head pain and sufferings.
b) TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioner has claimed compensation towards medical expenses.
The petitioner has produced Ex.P.11 - 4 medical bills for Rs.26,031/- and Ex.P.14 - 8 medical bills for Rs.15,461/-, in all at Rs.41,492/-.
It is the contention of the respondent No.2 that, amount towards medical bills were given by the NGO and the employer.
But to prove the same, respondent No.2 has not taken any steps.

Therefore, it has been considered as there is SCCH - 9 11 MVC No.3886/2021 no dispute about these medical bills, the Tribunal is of the view that petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.41,492/- is just and reasonable towards Medical Expenses.
c) TOWARDS FOOD, EXTRA NOURISHMENT, CONVEYANCE AND MEDICAL ATTENDANT CHARGES:
On perusal of records, petitioner has produced discharge summary marked at Ex.P.13.
On perusal of Ex.P.13 it came to know that, petitioner took treatment for only one day.
Therefore, Considering the said fact the Tribunal is of the view that petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,000/- towards food extra nourishment, conveyance and medical attendant.
d) TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:

The petitioner contended that she was working as a fund riser in NGO and getting salary of Rs.23,000/- per month and she took leave for 3 months without pay and now she is in continuing service but she is not able to do job as before the accident.
To prove SCCH - 9 12 MVC No.3886/2021 the income, petitioner has not produced any document.
Hence, to fix the income of the petitioner, lets rely on the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, which fixed notional income of the year 2023 at 16,000/- p.m.
Accordingly, the notional income of petitioner during the year 2021 treated as Rs.15,000/- p.m.,

During cross examination of petitioner,
she has admitted that, for 3 months she has not get salary.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case this tribunal held that petitioner might have taken 3 months rest.

Hence,
petitioner is entitled to Rs.45,000/- (Rs.15,000/- x 3) towards loss of income during laid up period.
e) Towards Future Earnings:
The petitioner has contended that due to accident she was inpatient in the hospital and has become permanently disabled.
Moreover, the petitioner has not examined the doctor about assessment of disability.
Moreover as she contended that, she has continued her work.
Therefore, the question does not arise to award under the loss of future earning capacity.

Therefore,
the petitioner is not SCCH - 9 13 MVC No.3886/2021 entitled any compensation under the head of loss of future earning capacity.

5 f) Towards Deprivation of future Amenities:

The petitioner has contended that, on account of the said injuries occurred in RTA, she has not able to bite hard food one teeth was broken, some teeth are shaking not able to breath normally, pain occurred in her right knee.

Hence she has not able to walk as normally, she has not able to lift small and heavy weight, not able to climb stair, pain occurred on face and head, chest not able to sleep as normal and pain near right eye.
As per wound certificate she sustained simple injury as well as grievous injury.

By considering the facts and circumstances of the case the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of Rs.50,000/- is just and reasonable towards under the head of deprivation of future amenities.
g) FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
Petitioner has not deposed with regard to the future medication therefore, she is not entitled for any compensation SCCH - 9 14 MVC No.3886/2021 under the head future medical expenses.

13. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:

 suffering  b. Towards medical expenses .41,492/-
 c. Towards food and extra .4,000/-
 nourishment, conveyance  and medical attendant  d. Towards loss of income .45,000/-
 during laid up period  e. Towards loss of future --  earning  f. Towards future amenities .50,000/-
 g. Towards future medical --  expenses

Total compensation .1,70,492/-
14.
Regarding Liability:
As already stated above the petitioner has proved that the accident in question was caused by the driver of the Baleno Alpha Car bearing reg.No.KA-53-MG-0063 with rash and negligent act.
It is the contention of the respondent No.2 that, the complaint lodged after lapse of 6 days.
Again to prove the same, respondent No.2 has not taken any sort of steps.
SCCH - 9 15 MVC No.3886/2021 Therefore, the respondent No.1 & 2 being the R.C.owner and insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the respondent No.2 being the insurer of offending vehicle is primarily liable to pay the compensation with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
Accordingly, I answered Issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative.
15. ISSUE NO.3:

In view of my finding on issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The petition filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

6
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of .1,70,492/- (Rupees one lakh seventy thousand four hundred ninety two only) with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

However, SCCH - 9 16 MVC No.3886/2021 in view of the policy, the respondent No.2/insurance company is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner and directed to deposit the compensation amount in this tribunal within one month from the date of this order.
After deposit of compensation amount, the entire amount with accrued interest shall be released on proper identification through e-payment.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
